previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for her 21st cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She experienced mild nausea and insomnia with racing thoughts during the first night but remained otherwise stable. Methotrexate was administered safely with IV bicarbonate for urine alkalinization and fosaprepitant for nausea prophylaxis, avoiding Zofran due to prior headaches. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, reaching 0.18 micromolar by discharge. A surveillance brain MRI showed no new or enhancing lesions, with only stable chronic changes. She remained neurologically intact, and her chronic conditions, including depression, asthma, ulcerative colitis, and right leg pain, were managed without complication. Aspirin was held during admission with heparin bridging for DVT prophylaxis and was restarted at discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with a short course of oral leucovorin and instructions to resume her baseline medications.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for cycle 23 of HD MTX. After 
alkalinization of her urine per the usual protocol she was given 
methotrexate IV 8000mg/m2 for a total dose of 13760mg. She had 
nausea and vomiting for most of the following day but by 
discharge was symptom free and able to tolerate a regular diet. 
Urine pH was maintained above 8 and leucovorin rescue was 
started 24 hours after completion of methotrexate. At discharge 
her methotrexate level is 0.03. She will return in 1 month for 
her next cycle. Prescription refill for ativan was given.
